resolution.detail: All seven distributions contain only Token cards (TKN1/TKN2/TKN3/TKN4 series; the San Diego Comic-Con page is literally a redirect to the Orichalcos Challenge token). Tokens are game aids with no deck legality and no passcodes; they cannot enter any card pool.

The eight cards the importer could not match to BabelCDB are all one-of-a-kind World Championship match-winner prizes (2004-2007) or the WC2007 event-exclusive Spell 'Get Your Game On!' (whose own text restricts play to attendees of that event). None has a passcode; none was ever tournament legal. The lone tournament-legal match winner in history, Victory Dragon, was a normal Shonen Jump promo (not in this family) and was Forbidden about two months after release.

Each set is the year's World Championship winner prizes: one-of-a-kind English match-winner cards (Xexex/Eternia 2005; Testament/Armament 2006; Chimaera/Emperor of Lightning + the event-exclusive 'Get Your Game On!' 2007; Tyr/Lorelei 2008; Aggiba/Skuna 2009; Stardust Divinity/Grizzly 2010) plus an Asian-English reprint of a prior prize. Match winners carry printed limitation text ('This card cannot be used in a Duel'), have no passcodes (absent from BabelCDB; YGOPRODeck uses synthetic ids), and were never tournament legal; the Asian-English prints are OCG-backed and were banned from TCG play throughout the era per UDE Appendix A. No card in these products can enter any TCG pool.

subjects: Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters National Tournament prize cards (top-placer tier)

resolution.detail: The top-4/top-3/runner-up/winner tier of the National Tournament (held February 1-21, 1999) awarded four one-of-a-kind stainless-steel metal cards - "Black Luster Soldier" (1 copy, winner only), "Zera the Mant" (2 copies), "Super War-Lion" (3 copies), "Fiend's Mirror" (4 copies) - none of which was ever otherwise available; per Yugipedia none were reprinted until a 2023 promotion (Black Luster Soldier only). These are one-of-a-kind competition trophies, not a public or repeatable release, matching this dataset's existing gap-wc-prize-products precedent for the same category of item. "Black Luster Soldier" specifically is additionally a genuinely distinct historical identity from the modern Ritual Monster of the same name (BabelCDB records it as passcode 10000100, a >10-distance/"far" alias of the modern card's 5405694, i.e. its own canonical card, not an artwork variant) - using the modern card's passcode for this 1999 Normal Monster prize print would misrepresent it, so no passcode is recorded for it at all rather than inventing or misapplying one. "Zera the Mant" and "Super War-Lion" resolve to their sole/modern BabelCDB passcodes with no historical variant recorded, and "Fiend's Mirror" has no BabelCDB entry referenced anywhere else in this dataset; none is used because the whole tier is excluded on availability grounds regardless of identity resolvability.
